note: Read 2026-11-04 by the research of a series and a play in every market (scratchpad l4t: the first wave t1-t8 and the follow-up u1-u25, merged item by item, the later verdict standing where it read more): what a series' and a play's producer can draw on there. Each quote kept was found in its saved file (the integrator's check, 2026-11-04); a quote not found there was left out, and a figure with none left was left out with it. Attempts recorded for a web search the shared allowance refused were dropped, not being attempts.

sources.title: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 (Cth), compilation in force from 1 October 2026, volume 7, Division 376 (Federal Register of Legislation)
sources.said: The amount of the producer offset is: … (a)if the *film is a *feature film that was produced for commercial exhibition to the public in cinemas—40%; or … (b)otherwise—30%; … (ii)each episode of the series is at least one half of a commercial hour in duration, except where the film is predominantly made using cell, stop motion, digital or other animation, in which case each episode is at least one quarter of a commercial hour in duration; and … A *film where the application for the certificate is for a series and not for a season of that series, and the series is not a *documentary … $1 million … $500,000 … duration of film in hours means the total length of the *film, measured in hours.

sources.title: ITAA 1997 Div 376 (as item 1)
sources.said: (ii) remuneration provided to the principal director, producers and principal cast associated with the film; to the extent that such expenditure comprises greater than 20% of the company’s * total film expenditure on the film

sources.title: Screen Australia: Narrative Content Production Funding Guidelines
sources.said: television projects must have a contingency of 8% of below-the-line

sources.title: Creative Australia: Arts Projects for Individuals and Groups
sources.said: Funding of between $10,000 and $50,000 for a range of activities and projects, both national and international, across all arts practices. … Applications close: Tuesday 1 September 2026 … You must be an Australian citizen or an Australian permanent resident, and a practicing artist or arts professional. … How competitive are your grants rounds? As a national arts funding body, all our grant rounds are competitive. Success rates are usually between 10% and 15%.

figures.finding: A series on Norfolk Island is Australia's: the producer offset, 30% for a series (40% only for a cinema feature). The 'significant Australian content' test (s 376-65) also applies; not quoted here. These are Australia's series terms and belong with AU's research too.

au.fundedSeriesNeeds: a local commissioning platform and a rest-of-world distributor

sources.said: For episodic or feature length projects for which Television (including SVOD or BVOD) is the first and primary window, applicants must: o have a local commissioning platform secured on terms acceptable to Screen Australia, including meeting the following minimum licence fee requirements*, … a confirmed minimum licence fee of $550,000 per broadcast hour allocated toward the initial licence period (3 years) against the primary right … for Children’s content, a confirmed minimum of: • $125,000 per broadcast half hour for one commissioning platform with limited exclusivity holdbacks; or • $144,000 for (i) combination of commissioning platforms; or (ii) one commissioning platform with full exclusivity … o have secured a ROW Distributor with a letter of offer (LOO) … the first funding decision within the updated minimum licence fee requirements being in force from 1 July 2026
